questions: Did these abnormal movements begin suddenly?
Are the movements involuntary?
Do they occur only in your right arm and hand?
Are the movements present when your arm is completely at rest?
Can you temporarily stop the movements when you concentrate?
Do the movements disappear when you are asleep?
Have the movements been progressively worsening?
Do you have weakness or numbness on either side of your body?
Have you had any facial drooping, difficulty speaking, confusion, or trouble understanding speech?
Have you had a sudden severe headache, vision loss, dizziness, or difficulty walking?
Have you lost awareness, blacked out, or had a seizure?
Do you have neck, shoulder, arm, or hand pain?
Did this start after an injury, infection, or medical procedure?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Are you taking medications for nausea, depression, psychosis, seizures, Parkinson’s disease, or sleep?
Have you used recreational drugs or been exposed to toxins recently?
Have you had similar movements before?
Does anyone in your family have tremor, dystonia, Huntington’s disease, or another movement disorder?
Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, liver disease, or a history of stroke?
Have you had fever, unexplained weight loss, or night sweats?

results: 1. Comprehensive bedside neurological examination with distraction, entrainment, suggestibility, and dual-task manoeuvres
mental status / cognitive screen: progressive disorientation, tangential speech, grandiose hallucinations and euphoric affect
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): hemichorea affecting one side
distribution of the movements (one side, both, face, limbs): not characterised
effect of voluntary action and anxiety: no clear change
2. Bedside cranial-nerve, facial-movement, language, and speech examination
3. MRI of the brain with and without contrast
brain MRI with contrast: 1.5T with gadolinium - frontal-predominant atrophy but NO focal lesion, with normal basal ganglia structure and volume
4. Complete blood count, comprehensive metabolic panel, glucose, calcium, magnesium, phosphate, thyroid-stimulating hormone, vitamin B12, and folate
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
serum calcium, magnesium and phosphate: normal
6. Surface electromyography and accelerometry during the abnormal movements
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Huntington disease caused by a pathogenic CAG-repeat expansion in the HTT gene (a likely de novo expansion given the absent family history)

ALTERNATIVE: Autoimmune encephalitis–associated chorea, particularly anti-NMDA-receptor encephalitis

ALTERNATIVE: Wilson disease due to pathogenic biallelic ATP7B variants

ALTERNATIVE: Neuroacanthocytosis due to a VPS13A-related disorder
